proposals.name: arkts-strict-mode-pitfall-checklist
proposals.description: Fix-map for recurring ArkTS strict-mode compile traps (catch annotation, static-this, index signature, untyped literals, asset placement) — apply fix, no exploration.
proposals.skill_md:
# ArkTS strict-mode pitfall checklist

Apply the matching fix directly; do not explain or explore.

- `catch (e: Error)` → `catch (e)` — type annotations forbidden in catch
- static method using `this` → module-level singleton object
- index signature / `obj[key]` → `Map<string,T>` + `.get()` — only compliant dynamic lookup; class field tables too
- `{x} as Record` still untyped → declare real `interface` with named fields
- Alignment/enum member → confirm exists via harmony_api_lookup before writing
- new SVG/icon asset → `rawfile/`, not `media/`
- CRLF/LF mixed file → normalize LF before edit; if edit_file state desyncs after a node script pass, use flexReplace-tolerant match
- Web component options (e.g. `incognitoMode`) → constructor params, not chained properties; check getRequestUrl/getRequestMethod signatures
- CJK inside `node -e` inline in cmd → write_file a .cjs, then run it

Rule: batch fixes, then ONE build; on error grep this list before any new investigation.

proposals.name: arkui-reactive-refresh-pitfalls
proposals.description: Fix-map for ArkUI silent non-refresh: struct private getters dropped by ForEach/@Builder, @Builder value-param caching, stale field-initializer arrays.
proposals.skill_md:
# ArkUI silent refresh failures — fix map

Symptom: data is alive (logs/SSE) but UI blank, stale, or items missing after a state change (locale switch, menu, sidebar).

- struct `private get X()` consumed by ForEach/@Builder → children silently dropped. Fix: plain method `X()`. Then grep repo for remaining `private get` inside structs — same bug repeats.
- @Builder receiving an evaluated value (e.g. `Icon(I18n.t('k'))`) → arg cached, never re-passed. Fix: pass the key, evaluate inside the builder.
- field-initializer arrays calling I18n.t()/lookups → evaluated once at construction. Fix: convert to methods/getters so each render re-evaluates.
- no re-render trigger → add anchor: `@StorageProp('x_version') @Watch` bump int; bind a `<0` fake node on the affected subtree.
- i18n fallback check: `!== undefined`, never `.length > 0` (legal empty strings must not fall back).

Verify: one build + install + dumpLayout text audit (or hilog marker). No prose around the check.

proposals.name: arkui-i18n-refresh-regression-audit
proposals.description: Fix ArkUI screens that don't refresh after locale switch: render anchors, @Builder param caching, private-get child drop.
proposals.skill_md:
# ArkUI i18n Refresh Regression Audit

Locale switched but UI shows old language, blank menus, or collapsed children? Each failure class below has recurred 2+ times (P48→P49→P51). Apply silently, verify, report pass/fail only.

## Checklist
1. Missing render anchor: every component calling I18n.t needs
   @StorageProp('app_locale') @Watch('onLocale') appLocale: string = ''
   bump a localeVersion counter in onLocale; keep a fake dependency node
   (if (this.localeVersion < 0) { Text('') }) so the subtree re-renders.
2. @Builder/child VALUE params cache evaluated results:
   BAD:  RailIcon({ label: I18n.t('nav.home') })
   GOOD: RailIcon({ key: 'nav.home' }); inside child: Text(I18n.t(this.key))
3. private get consumed by ForEach/@Builder silently DROPS children:
   convert `private get items()` -> plain method `items()`.
4. Field-initializer arrays containing I18n.t() evaluate once at construction:
   move to methods recomputed on locale bump.
5. Fallback trap: use `!== undefined`, never `length > 0`
   (legit empty en strings must not fall back to zh).

## Verify
- Build + install, switch language in Settings.
- hdc shell uitest dumpLayout, grep a new-language-only string; 0 hits = regression.
- Re-check BOTH zh and en (past bugs passed zh, failed en).

Output: one line pass/fail + evidence path.

proposals.name: windows-cjk-script-file-not-inline
proposals.description: Run CJK-bearing node/python logic from a written script file, never inline; verify large write_file output with a check script.
proposals.skill_md:
# CJK Scripts: File, Not Inline (Windows)

Inline `node -e` / `python -c` containing CJK text garbles or crashes on Windows cmd. Write a file, run it, verify it.

## Rules
1. Any CJK in strings/keys/comments => write_file script.cjs, then
   run_command: node script.cjs
2. Large write_file (>300 lines, i18n packs, generated .ets) can inject tokens:
   write a check script and run it before building.
3. Script rewrites a file => read source fresh inside the script and assert
   non-empty before writing (target-as-source wipes files).
4. After a node script modified a file, edit_file state may drift:
   normalize CRLF->LF in the script or re-read before patching.

## Example
write_file p48_check.cjs:
  const s = require('fs').readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8');
  const m = s.match(/\["/g); if (!m || m.length < 100) process.exit(1);
run_command: node p48_check.cjs entry/src/main/ets/i18n/I18nZh.ets

On failure: fix and re-verify; report only pass/fail + file path.

proposals.description: when an acceptance/verification ping asks to reply with only a fixed acknowledgment token (e.g., 只回复两个字:收到) and forbids tool use, reply directly with that exact text
proposals.skill_md:
# Bare acknowledgment reply

1. Extract the requested acknowledgment token from the prompt, e.g. `只回复两个字:{{ack_text}}` -> answer token is `{{ack_text}}` (common values: 收到 / 明白 / 好的).
2. Honor the stated constraints: do NOT invoke any tools, do NOT read files, do NOT search, do NOT add explanations, markdown, quotes, or punctuation.
3. Compose the final message as exactly `{{ack_text}}` — nothing before or after it.
4. Send `{{ack_text}}` as the entire reply.
5. Scope check: only use this skill for direct-reply pings. If the message asks for real work (run a check, verify a build, inspect `{{artifact}}`, then acknowledge), fall back to the normal task flow and perform the requested action first.
6. If the ping's expected token differs from `{{ack_text}}`, always substitute the exact token written in that task's prompt, never a paraphrase.

proposals.name: kaihongos-release-hap-sign-recv-chain
proposals.description: Ship a KaihongOS release HAP when hvigorw output is rejected (install error 9568297): repack V1 STORED with mise python, sign device-side compatibleVersion 23, recv back, SHA256.
proposals.skill_md:
# KaihongOS release HAP: repack V1 → device sign → recv → hash

Trigger: hdc install rejects the hvigorw HAP with 9568297 (RestoolV2/API26 pack not accepted by device).

Chain — device only accepts the end product, no alternative route:
1. hvigorw assembleHap → product at entry\build\...\entry-default-unsigned.hap.
2. Repack V1 (STORED):
   C:\Users\hongfu\AppData\Local\mise\shims\python.exe tools\build_api23_hap.py <unsigned.hap>
3. Sign on device/VM side with hap-sign-tool, compatibleVersion 23 (existing pattern: install_pXX.py or pXX-sign-install.sh runs it where the SDK lives).
4. Install: `hdc -t <ip:port> install <signed.hap>`; confirm with `hdc shell bm dump -n <bundle>`.
5. Recover artifact: `hdc file recv /data/local/tmp/<signed.hap> release\`.
6. Manifest: `powershell Get-FileHash release\<signed.hap> -Algorithm SHA256`.

Rules:
- Never install or ship the step-1 hvigorw product directly.
- Never sign on host for this device — device-side signing is the known-good path.
- If install still fails 9568297, the pack is not V1 STORED; redo step 2 before any other triage.

proposals.name: windows-mise-python-shim-first
proposals.description: On this Windows host bare python/py resolve to the WindowsApps stub; invoke the mise shim path directly for every python script run.
proposals.skill_md:
# Windows python: mise shim, not the stub

Bare `python` / `py` resolve to the WindowsApps stub (silent no-op or Store popup). Do not probe, do not retry, do not switch interpreters.

1. Always invoke by full shim path:
   C:\Users\hongfu\AppData\Local\mise\shims\python.exe <script.py> <args>
2. Known consumers: tools\build_api23_hap.py, smoke_reg.py (pass --target <ip:port> explicitly), patch/verify scripts.
3. Single check if unsure: `C:\Users\hongfu\AppData\Local\mise\shims\python.exe --version` → 3.x real interpreter.
4. Shim missing → `mise which python`, or `mise x -- python <script.py>`.
5. Never chain through `py -3` or PATH-first python; a stub hit is not a retry signal.

proposals.name: fixed-token-reply-workflow
proposals.description: when a task instructs you to reply with only a fixed acknowledgment token (e.g., an acceptance check that forbids all tools), output exactly that token and nothing else
proposals.skill_md:
# Fixed-token reply routine

Trigger: user demands a bare, fixed reply token {{token}} (e.g., 收到) and explicitly forbids tool use.

## Steps
1. Extract the exact token the user requested: {{token}} (e.g., 收到).
2. Confirm constraints from the prompt: no tools, no extra text, direct reply.
3. Skip all normal agent behavior for this turn:
   - Do not call any tools, file reads, code search, or shell commands.
   - Do not run any other skill or workflow.
4. Emit the reply as plain text with exactly the requested token:

   {{token}}

5. Hard rules:
   - No explanations, no punctuation, no quotes, no markdown formatting.
   - No prefix (e.g., "Answer:") and no suffix (e.g., "done").
   - Character count must match the request (e.g., "two characters" → exactly {{token}}).
6. Stop after the token. Do not continue with related or follow-up actions.

## Parameter reference
- {{token}}: the literal token demanded by the user (收 to, OK, ACK, etc.)
